account:
Something beyond routine town business appears to be being arranged for eighteen hundred in the great hall. My written addendum calls it an approved lighting inspection with the builder, but I heard the builder ask neighbour to escort me there for a service acknowledgement. Neighbour agreed to accompany me, and secretary also says they will accompany me. Builder has specifically asked that the great hall door remain closed until the inspection. Together these details suggest a planned surprise acknowledgement or celebration for me, rather than just checking lights, though nobody has confirmed that outright.

There is also a community supper. Neighbour has solicited voluntary wheat or bread donations through freight, but said its time and venue were unconfirmed and did not name the organisers. Builder identifies innkeeper as coordinating hospitality. Several townsfolk report seeing innkeeper carrying a sack of bread, consistent with gathering food for a group. Baker, freight, builder and innkeeper have all been around town hall this afternoon; baker told freight to ask innkeeper to show the correct door. I suspect the supper and the great hall gathering are connected, but this remains an inference. My repeated questions to innkeeper have not yielded an intelligible answer.

Earlier reports of a bridge or port change were vague, and neighbour denied such a proposal. I have no solid evidence of any infrastructure change. Today's unusual activity looks more like preparations for a community event, possibly honouring my service, with details deliberately kept from me. Meanwhile my ordinary appointments remain in place: tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the hall at eighteen. Secretary confirms there are no council letters or petitions today.
